```{r}
library(DBI)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(noctua)
library(paws.storage)
library(readxl)

conn <- dbConnect(noctua::athena(), rstudio_conn_tab = FALSE)

run_query <- function(file) {
  sql <- paste(readLines(file), collapse = "\n")
  as_tibble(dbGetQuery(conn, sql))
}

# One row per PIN in the townships with reviewed sales, saying which
# characteristics differ between the 2025 and 2026 records
changes <- run_query("flag-review-changes.sql")
# One row per reviewed sale, with the analyst's flags
reviewed_sales <- run_query("flag-review-sales.sql")
# One row per 2025 sale in those townships
deviations <- run_query("flag-review-deviations.sql")
```

```{r}
# The table stores a blank workbook cell as "no", this is to get a more complete
# version of the analysis, since we don't store this information in the downstream athena tables,
# and I was curious about them explicitly writing "no" vs leaving it blank
s3 <- paws.storage::s3()
bucket <- "ccao-data-raw-us-east-1"
keys <- s3$list_objects_v2(Bucket = bucket, Prefix = "sale/flag_review/") |>
  getElement("Contents") |>
  sapply(\(object) object$Key)
keys <- keys[grepl("\\.xlsx$", keys)]

workbook_text <- lapply(keys, \(key) {
  path <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
  s3$download_file(Bucket = bucket, Key = key, Filename = path)
  sheet <- read_excel(path, col_types = "text")
  transmute(
    sheet,
    doc_no = `Sale Doc No`,
    source_file = basename(key),
    typed = toupper(trimws(`Characteristic Change`))
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  distinct(doc_no, source_file, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

```{r}
fields <- c(
  "Rooms" = "rooms",
  "Full baths" = "full_baths",
  "Beds" = "beds",
  "Central air" = "central_air",
  "Building sq ft" = "bldg_sf",
  "Basement finish" = "basement_finish",
  "Recent renovation" = "recent_renovation",
  "Half baths" = "half_baths",
  "Class" = "class",
  "Stories" = "stories",
  "Construction quality" = "construction_quality",
  "Attic finish" = "attic_finish",
  "Basement type" = "basement_type",
  "Exterior wall" = "exterior_wall",
  "Apartments" = "apartments"
)
changed_cols <- paste0(fields, "_changed")

# One workbook is left out of every chart. This is because it pre-dates our data input change that switched from char change 1/0 to char change maj/min/0, so it is harder to compare
pilot_workbook <- "valuations_sale_review_2025-12-16.xlsx"

pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
num <- function(x) prettyNum(x, big.mark = ",")

# 2025 review focused mainly on South with some of the highest SD sales from city
triads <- c("South", "City")

homes <- changes |>
  # A home with no card in both years has no field-by-field comparison. Count
  # those fields as unchanged; card_set_changed still marks the home as changed
  mutate(across(ends_with("_changed"), \(x) coalesce(x, FALSE))) |>
  mutate(
    any_changed = if_any(ends_with("_changed")),
    triad = factor(
      if_else(as.integer(township_code) >= 70, "City", "South"),
      levels = triads
    )
  )

# Reviewed sales of homes that have a residential record in either year.
reviewed <- reviewed_sales |>
  inner_join(homes, by = "pin") |>
  left_join(workbook_text, by = c("doc_no", "source_file")) |>
  mutate(
    typed = coalesce(typed, ""),
    not_arms_length = !is_arms_length,
    char_major = has_characteristic_change == "yes_major",
    char_minor = has_characteristic_change == "yes_minor",
    stored_no = has_characteristic_change == "no",
    char_no = stored_no & typed %in% c("NO", "N"),
    nothing_marked = is_arms_length & !is_flip & !has_class_change &
      char_no & !requires_field_check & !work_drawer
  )

main <- reviewed |>
  filter(source_file != pilot_workbook)

# The two comparison groups: homes with a 2025 sale the 2026 model trained on,
# and homes the 2026 model valued that did not sell in 2025. Neither includes
# a reviewed home
other_sales <- homes |>
  filter(trained_on_2025_sale, !pin %in% reviewed_sales$pin)
unsold <- homes |>
  filter(valued_by_2026_model, !sold_in_2025, !pin %in% reviewed_sales$pin)

# Reviewed sales against the two comparison groups, one set of rows per triad
groups <- lapply(triads, \(area) {
  like <- filter(main, triad == area)
  other <- filter(other_sales, triad == area)
  none <- filter(unsold, triad == area)
  tibble(
    triad = factor(area, levels = triads),
    label = c("Reviewed sales", "Other 2025 sales", "Homes with no 2025 sale"),
    n = c(nrow(like), nrow(other), nrow(none)),
    share = c(
      mean(like$any_changed), mean(other$any_changed), mean(none$any_changed)
    ),
    reviewed = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows()

# Look up one figure from `groups` for the text
group_share <- function(area, row) {
  pct(groups$share[groups$triad == area & groups$label == row])
}

# The flags, named with the labels shown in charts, then two comparison rows
flags <- c(
  "Class change" = "has_class_change",
  "Field check" = "requires_field_check",
  "Characteristic change: major" = "char_major",
  "Characteristic change: minor" = "char_minor",
  "Flip" = "is_flip",
  "Not arms-length" = "not_arms_length",
  "Work drawer" = "work_drawer"
)
comparison_rows <- c(
  "Analyst typed no characteristic change" = "char_no",
  "Nothing marked" = "nothing_marked"
)
flag_rows <- c(flags, comparison_rows)

# Share of reviewed sales with a change for each flag, by triad. `overall` is
# the share across both triads and sets the order of the rows
flag_rates <- lapply(names(flag_rows), \(label) {
  main |>
    filter(.data[[flag_rows[[label]]]]) |>
    mutate(overall = mean(any_changed)) |>
    group_by(triad, overall) |>
    summarise(n = n(), share = mean(any_changed), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(flag = label, is_flag = label %in% names(flags))
}) |>
  bind_rows()

# Price deviation bands, half a standard deviation wide. The tails are grouped
# because few sales sit that far out
band_edges <- seq(-2.5, 2, 0.5)
edge_text <- sub("-", "\u2212", sapply(band_edges, format))
band_labels <- c(
  paste("Below", edge_text[1]),
  paste(head(edge_text, -1), "to", tail(edge_text, -1)),
  paste(tail(edge_text, 1), "or more")
)

# 2025 sales with a price deviation, reviewed or not.
banded <- deviations |>
  inner_join(homes, by = "pin") |>
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      doc_no %in% main$doc_no ~ "Reviewed sales",
      pin %in% other_sales$pin ~ "Other 2025 sales"
    ),
    group = factor(group, levels = c("Reviewed sales", "Other 2025 sales")),
    band = cut(
      price_deviation,
      breaks = c(-Inf, band_edges, Inf), labels = band_labels, right = FALSE
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(group))

# One chart panel per triad and group
band_panels <- banded |>
  count(group, triad) |>
  mutate(
    panel = paste0(triad, ": ", tolower(group), " (n = ", num(n), ")"),
    panel = factor(panel, levels = panel)
  ) |>
  select(group, triad, panel)

by_band <- banded |>
  group_by(group, triad, band) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    across(all_of(c("any_changed", changed_cols)), mean),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  inner_join(band_panels, by = c("group", "triad"))

# Put under every chart
period <- "2025 sales. Records compared between tax years 2025 and 2026"
```

```{r}
# Chart styling shared by every figure
blue <- "#2a78d6"
gray <- "#b4b3ad"
ink <- "#0b0b0b"
muted <- "#52514e"

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "#e7e6e1", linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_text(colour = ink),
      axis.text.x = element_text(colour = muted),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = muted, size = 12),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 13),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
)

# Horizontal bars with the value and sample size written at the end of each
# bar. `data` needs the columns label, share, n, and reviewed (TRUE for blue,
# FALSE for gray). `reference` holds shares to mark with a dashed line
bar_chart <- function(data, limit, breaks = waiver(), reference = NULL) {
  reference_line <- if (!is.null(reference)) {
    geom_vline(
      data = reference,
      aes(xintercept = share), linetype = "dashed", colour = ink
    )
  }

  ggplot(data, aes(share, label, fill = reviewed)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.6) +
    reference_line +
    # A white box behind each label keeps the dashed line from running
    # through it
    geom_label(
      aes(label = paste0(" ", pct(share), " (n = ", num(n), ")")),
      hjust = 0, colour = ink, size = 4, fill = "white",
      border.colour = NA, label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines")
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = blue, "FALSE" = gray)) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = scales::label_percent(),
      breaks = breaks,
      limits = c(0, limit),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
    )
}

# Put bars in the order given, top to bottom
in_order <- function(x) factor(x, levels = rev(unique(x)))

# A grid of shares with the value written in each cell. `data` needs the
# columns share and text, and `x` and `y` name the columns to put on each axis
heatmap <- function(data, x, y) {
  ggplot(data, aes({{ x }}, {{ y }}, fill = share)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1.5) +
    geom_text(
      aes(
        label = text,
        colour = !is.na(share) & share > 0.8 * max(share, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      size = 4
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = c("#f3f8fe", "#cde2fb", "#86b6ef", "#3987e5", "#1c5cab"),
      limits = c(0, NA), na.value = "white"
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "white", "FALSE" = ink)) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(colour = ink, face = "bold", lineheight = 0.9)
    )
}
```

## Main findings

```{r}
# Figures quoted in the findings below
group_n <- function(area, row) {
  num(groups$n[groups$triad == area & groups$label == row])
}

# Share changed in each price deviation band for one triad and group of sales
band_shares <- function(area, sales) {
  rows <- filter(by_band, triad == area, group == sales)
  setNames(rows$any_changed, rows$band)
}
south_reviewed <- band_shares("South", "Reviewed sales")
south_other <- band_shares("South", "Other 2025 sales")[names(south_reviewed)]
city_reviewed <- band_shares("City", "Reviewed sales")

# Reviewed sales with a sales validation standard deviation of 1 or more
high_share <- function(area) {
  high <- filter(
    banded, group == "Reviewed sales", triad == area, price_deviation >= 1
  )
  pct(mean(high$any_changed))
}

workbooks <- function(area) n_distinct(main$source_file[main$triad == area])
```

- **In the South, a reviewed sale was more likely to get a characteristic
  update than a sale that was not reviewed.**
  `r group_share("South", "Reviewed sales")` of reviewed sales had a change,
  against `r group_share("South", "Other 2025 sales")` of other 2025 sales. The
  gap holds across price deviation bands. Reviewed sales changed more often in
  `r sum(south_reviewed > south_other)` of the `r length(south_reviewed)`
  bands, though the size of the gap varies and is near zero in a few of them.
- **South sales that were not reviewed still changed often.**
  `r group_share("South", "Other 2025 sales")` of them changed, against
  `r group_share("South", "Homes with no 2025 sale")` of South homes with no
  2025 sale. Other characteristic update workflows may account for some of
  this.
- **Sales with high sales validation standard deviation values changed most,
  but changes are spread across the whole range.** Among reviewed sales with a
  sales validation standard deviation of 1 or more, `r high_share("South")`
  changed in the South and `r high_share("City")` in the City. No band is close
  to zero. The lowest band for reviewed sales is `r pct(min(south_reviewed))`
  in the South and `r pct(min(city_reviewed))` in the City.
- **The City has fewer reviewed sales and a much lower baseline.** The City has
  `r group_n("City", "Reviewed sales")` reviewed sales and the South has
  `r group_n("South", "Reviewed sales")`. Only
  `r group_share("City", "Other 2025 sales")` of other 2025 sales in the City
  changed, and `r group_share("City", "Homes with no 2025 sale")` of homes with
  no sale. The City was not reassessed in 2026, which is the likely reason.
  Reviewed City sales still changed
  `r group_share("City", "Reviewed sales")` of the time.
- **All City reviews came from one workbook.** The City review was completed by
  one analyst. The South reviews are spread across `r workbooks("South")` workbooks
  from several analysts.

## Which flags correlate with characteristic changes?

```{r}

flag_rates |>
  arrange(desc(overall)) |>
  mutate(label = in_order(flag), reviewed = is_flag) |>
  bar_chart(
    limit = 1.25, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
    reference = filter(groups, label == "Other 2025 sales")
  ) +
  facet_wrap(vars(triad)) +
  theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(2, "lines")) +

```

## Which characteristics changed?

```{r}
#| fig-height: 14
# One column per group of homes in each triad, titled with its sample size
field_columns <- function(area) {
  like <- filter(main, triad == area)
  other <- filter(other_sales, triad == area)
  subsets <- list(
    "All\nreviewed" = like,
    "Class\nchange" = filter(like, has_class_change),
    "Field\ncheck" = filter(like, requires_field_check),
    "Char. change:\nmajor" = filter(like, char_major),
    "Char. change:\nminor" = filter(like, char_minor),
    "Flip" = filter(like, is_flip)
  )
  reviewed_columns <- lapply(names(subsets), \(column) {
    tibble(
      group = column,
      n = nrow(subsets[[column]]),
      field = names(fields),
      share = colMeans(subsets[[column]][changed_cols])
    )
  })
  other_column <- tibble(
    group = "Other 2025\nsales",
    n = nrow(other),
    field = names(fields),
    share = colMeans(other[changed_cols])
  )
  bind_rows(other_column, reviewed_columns) |>
    mutate(triad = factor(area, levels = triads))
}

by_field <- lapply(triads, field_columns) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(column = paste0(group, "\nn = ", num(n)))

# Fields run top to bottom from most to least often changed on reviewed sales
field_order <- names(fields)[order(colMeans(main[changed_cols]))]

by_field |>
  mutate(
    column = factor(column, levels = unique(column)),
    field = factor(field, levels = field_order),
    text = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * share)
  ) |>
  heatmap(column, field) +
  facet_wrap(vars(triad), ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", panel.spacing.y = unit(2, "lines")) +
  labs(
    title = "Share of homes where each characteristic changed (%)",
    subtitle = period
  )
```

## Does a sale's price deviation correlate with characteristic changes?

```{r}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 9
by_band |>
  mutate(
    label = factor(band, levels = band_labels),
    share = any_changed,
    reviewed = group == "Reviewed sales"
  ) |>
  bar_chart(limit = 1.05, breaks = seq(0, 0.75, 0.25)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel), ncol = 2) +
  theme(
    panel.spacing.x = unit(2, "lines"),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(1.5, "lines"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(colour = muted, margin = margin(r = 10))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste(
      "Share of sales with any characteristic changed,",
      "by price deviation"
    ),
    subtitle = paste0(period, ". n is the number of sales"),
    y = "Standard deviations above or below the price of similar sales"
  )
```

The next chart splits the same sales by characteristic. Where characteristic
changes rise with price, the characteristics that changed are mostly rooms, full
baths, and beds. The top row of each panel is the number of sales in the band,
and bands with few sales give noisy shares.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 17
# A top row holds the number of sales in each band
sales_row <- "Number of sales"

band_fields <- lapply(names(fields), \(name) {
  tibble(
    panel = by_band$panel,
    band = by_band$band,
    field = name,
    share = by_band[[paste0(fields[[name]], "_changed")]],
    text = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * share)
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows()

band_counts <- by_band |>
  transmute(panel, band, field = sales_row, share = NA_real_, text = num(n))

bind_rows(band_fields, band_counts) |>
  mutate(field = factor(field, levels = c(field_order, sales_row))) |>
  heatmap(band, field) +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel), ncol = 2, axes = "all_x") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top", labels = scales::label_wrap(6)) +
  theme(
    strip.placement = "outside",
    panel.spacing.x = unit(1.5, "lines"),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(2, "lines"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste(
      "Share of sales where each characteristic changed,",
      "by price deviation (%)"
    ),
    subtitle = paste0(
      period, ".\nEach column is a price deviation band, in standard ",
      "deviations from the price of similar sales. Darker means changed more ",
      "often"
    )
  )
```
